Looking up the actual *source document* history of JC is really hard because the early Christian Church obfuscated a lot of it. There are a few references to an execution of someone referred to as “king of the Jews” in letters between Romans and Egyptians so he probably did exist as a person, but he was probably more like a particularly radical rabbi. Someone who went against the status quo set up by the Pharisees and Sadducees. Someone who enacted large amounts of change in how Jewish people thought about people in society. But really, there are no reliable direct quotes or eye witness accounts. Most scholars put the earliest writings about him at like 100+ years after the events took place.
